questions: Does the operation allow deleting any occurrence of the substring "()" regardless of nesting depth, or must the parentheses be matched as a proper pair in the usual bracket-matching sense?
Are the other bracket types ([], <>) ever removable, or are they only allowed to appear as part of the definition of a “colorful” sequence without being directly deleted?
If multiple disjoint substrings "()" exist simultaneously, may we choose any one of them in each operation, and does the choice affect the answer?
Must the deletions be performed strictly one at a time, or can we delete several non‑overlapping "()" substrings in a single step?
Is the empty string considered a colorful bracket sequence (i.e., should we output “Yes” for S = "")?
Are there any restrictions on the total number of operations (e.g., must it be ≤ |S|) or can we perform an arbitrary number of deletions until no "()" remains?
Should the output be exactly “Yes”/“No” with that capitalization and no extra whitespace or newline characters?
Are there any hidden constraints on the input size beyond the given length (e.g., memory limits) that could affect the choice of algorithm?

inline_prompts: You are given a string S consisting of six types of characters: (, ), [, ], <, >. A string T is called a colorful bracket sequence if it satisfies the following condition: It is possible to turn T into an empty string by repeating the following operation any number of times (possibly zero): - If there exists a contiguous substring of T that is one of (), choose one such substring and delete it. - If the deleted substring was at the beginning or end of T, the remainder becomes the new T. - Otherwise, concatenate the part before the deleted substring and the part after the deleted substring, and that becomes the new T.
